scenes.heading: Star Schema
scenes.narration: A star schema organizes analytical data into one central fact table surrounded by descriptive dimension tables.

scenes.heading: Why it shines for analytics
bullets: One fact table holds measurable events and numbers.
Dimensions describe the who, what, when, and where.
Simple structure is easy for BI tools to query.
scenes.narration: The fact table stores the measurable events, like sales amounts, while the dimensions give them context such as product, date, and store. Because dimensions are denormalized, queries touch fewer tables and run faster. That simplicity is exactly why business intelligence tools love star schemas.

scenes.heading: Shape of the star
scenes.narration: At the center sits the fact table, holding one row per business event. Its foreign keys radiate outward, each pointing to a dimension that describes an aspect of that event. Analysts join the fact to whichever dimensions their question needs, producing the classic star shape.

scenes.heading: A star join in practice
scenes.code:
SELECT d.product_name,
       t.year,
       SUM(f.sales_amount) AS revenue
FROM   fact_sales   f
JOIN   dim_product  d ON f.product_key = d.product_key
JOIN   dim_time     t ON f.time_key    = t.time_key
GROUP BY d.product_name, t.year;
scenes.narration: This query joins the sales fact to the product and time dimensions to total revenue by product and year. Notice the fact supplies the numbers while the dimensions supply the labels. Because there are only two joins from a single hub, the query stays fast and readable.

scenes.heading: Normalized vs star
scenes.narration: A transactional database normalizes aggressively to avoid update anomalies. A star schema deliberately denormalizes dimensions to make reporting simple and fast. You trade some storage and update complexity for query speed, which is the right trade for analytics.

scenes.text: A star schema keeps facts at the center and descriptive dimensions around them, giving fast, intuitive analytical queries.
scenes.narration: When your goal is reporting rather than transactions, the star schema's simple hub-and-spoke design pays off every day.
